title: San Francisco supes hit pause on new data centers
source_used: The San Francisco Standard; text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-09.txt
key_facts: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 for a 45-day moratorium on data centers.
It pauses city approvals and tasks the Planning Department with studying impacts and drafting long-term controls.
The moratorium awaits action from the mayor; an earlier version of the article wrongly said it took effect immediately (a correction was added).
It could be extended to 22 months, but it is unclear whether city leaders would consider that.
Supervisor Shamann Walton, who wrote it, lists energy, water, air quality, land use and community impacts as issues to study.
A hearing on the Planning Department's findings is due by November.
Oakley, Richmond and Gilroy already have moratoriums; Oakland and Hayward are considering them.
San Francisco has six data center sites, two in Walton's district, per Data Center Map.
quote_evidence: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors on Tuesday unanimously approved a 45-day moratorium on data centers that would pause city approvals of the facilities and task the Planning Department with studying their impacts and developing long-term controls.
The moratorium could be extended to 22 months, but it’s unclear whether city leaders would entertain the idea.
The cities of Oakley, Richmond, and Gilroy already have moratoriums on data centers, while Oakland and Hayward are considering it.
why_it_matters_hint: Another big US city is pausing data center approvals while it studies their effects.
notes: The article carries a correction: the moratorium is not yet in force and awaits the mayor.
